claim: F(G) = N-3  <=>  G is distance-hereditary (rank-width 1; C5-vertex-minor-free)

fable_conjecture.check_recipe: Given a representative graph G: (1) verify G is connected; (2) apply the pruning algorithm: while |V|>1, find a pendant vertex (degree 1), a pair of true twins (adjacent, N[u]=N[v]), or a pair of false twins (non-adjacent, N(u)=N(v)), and delete one vertex of the pair (or the pendant); if the graph reduces to a single vertex, output EXTREMAL, else (no reduction applies while |V|>1) output NOT EXTREMAL. Equivalent O(n^5) brute-force check: G is extremal iff it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the house, the gem, the domino, or any cycle C_k with k ≥ 5. Equivalent third check: compute rank-width (or verify cut-rank ≤ 1 split decomposition into stars and cliques); extremal iff rank-width ≤ 1, i.e., the split decomposition of G has only complete and star components.
fable_conjecture.confidence: high — the class fits all 44 orbits exactly, is provably LC/vertex-minor invariant (Bouchet, Oum), has a natural single excluded vertex-minor (C5) matching the observed obstructions (every non-extremal orbit exhibits an induced C5 or house), and rank-width 1 is precisely the structural condition enabling tree-like (split/GHZ) decompositions of graph states, giving a physical mechanism for attaining the N-3 fusion floor. Expected to generalize to the held-out n=8,9 orbits.
fable_conjecture.defining_property: A connected graph G is distance-hereditary iff every connected induced subgraph preserves all pairwise distances of G (d_H(u,v)=d_G(u,v) for every connected induced H). Equivalent characterizations: (1) G has rank-width at most 1 (cut-rank over GF(2) of one side of every branch of some branch-decomposition is ≤ 1); (2) G contains no induced house, gem, domino, or cycle of length ≥ 5; (3) G has no vertex-minor isomorphic to C5 (Oum); (4) G can be reduced to a single vertex by repeatedly deleting pendant vertices, true twins, or false twins. Conjecture: an LC-orbit is extremal (F = N-3) iff its graphs are distance-hereditary.
fable_conjecture.discriminating_evidence: Smallest discriminator: n=5 id 6 is exactly the house graph (C5 plus one chord, the LC-orbit of the 5-cycle) — the unique non-DH orbit among the four n=5 orbits — while the three extremal n=5 orbits (join(K2,E3), wheel W4, double star) are DH. At n=6: non-extremal id 15 has induced C5 on {0,2,4,1,3}, id 16 has induced C5 on {2,0,5,4,1}, id 17 has induced house on {0,1,4,3,5}; the 8 extremal n=6 orbits include K3,3 (id 8), octahedron K2,2,2 (id 13), W4+pendant (id 12), all DH. At n=7 all 11 non-extremal orbits contain an induced C5 (ids 33: {1,5,3,6,4}; 34: {0,5,1,4,6}; 40: {0,2,1,3,4}) or an induced house (ids 35,36,37,38,39,41,42,43, e.g. id 38 on {0,5,6,1,3}, id 43 on {0,2,1,4,6}), while all 15 extremal n=7 orbits reduce fully by pendant/twin elimination (e.g., id 24 = K3,4, id 26 = complement of K3∪K2∪K2, id 31 = K2,2,2 + pendant). The classification fits all 44/44 orbits with zero exceptions.
fable_conjecture.graph_class_name: Distance-hereditary graphs (equivalently: connected graphs of rank-width 1; C5-vertex-minor-free graphs)
fable_conjecture.lc_invariant_justification: Distance-hereditariness is a genuine LC-orbit invariant on two independent grounds: (a) Bouchet (1987/1988, 'Transforming trees by successive local complementations' and related isotropic-systems work) proved that the class of distance-hereditary graphs is closed under local complementation; (b) Oum (2005, 'Rank-connectivity and vertex-minors') proved that rank-width (cut-rank over GF(2)) is invariant under local complementation, and that connected graphs of rank-width ≤ 1 are exactly the distance-hereditary graphs. Moreover the class is vertex-minor closed with the unique excluded vertex-minor C5, so membership depends only on the LC orbit — consistent with the data, where each non-extremal representative exhibits some member of the house/C5 family (all LC-equivalent obstructions).
fable_conjecture.summary: The extremal LC-orbits (attaining the universal minimum F(G)=N-3 in the GHZ3 fusion model) are exactly the orbits of distance-hereditary graphs, equivalently the connected graphs of rank-width 1, equivalently the graphs with no vertex-minor isomorphic to C5. All 30 extremal representatives in the catalog are distance-hereditary (trees, cographs such as K3,3, K3,4, K2,2,2, wheels W4, joins K1/K2 with complete-bipartite or edgeless graphs, plus pendant attachments), while every one of the 14 non-extremal representatives contains an induced C5 or house (id 6 IS the house = LC-orbit of C5; ids 15,16,33,34,40 contain induced C5; ids 17,35,36,37,38,39,41,42,43 contain induced houses).
